pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/27627
Regressed with https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/27454

Previous logic was not utilizing command's `StartValue`, which can make sprite visible again if not zero.

review_comments:
Shouldn't this be `Math.Max(deathTImes[0], alphaCommand.EndTime)` for safety or something?

Also goes for every single similar usage pattern below.

As far as my understanding goes, no. Since commands are ordered by the start time and new command will apply start value immediately - it will be overriden regardless of the length of the previous commands and there's no reason to compare new time with the saved one.
Example:
```
F,0,0,10000,0,1 // Fade from 0 to 1 starting from 0 with 10s duration
F,0,1000,2000,1,0 // Fade from 1 to 0 starting from 1s with 1s duration
```
Even if the 1st command is 10s long and 2nd command starts while 1st is active, 2nd command will become active at 1s mark and after that there's no need to keep track of the 1st one.
With my implementation end time will be 2000, while with yours optimisation will be skipped completely `Max(double.MaxValue, 2000) = double.MaxValue`
I'm gonna have to go cross-check stable to confirm that.

> So I cross-checked stable and what you say is pretty blatantly false

I never said a word about stable. Stable does handle concurent transforms differently and that's [a separate issue](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/7257#issuecomment-567844226). My approach aims for the lazer transforms (the way they are implemented currently). Though I'm not against fixing those first and then looking into optimizing and leaving this pr on-hold until then. Or may be better yet just revert my older changes since they are pretty isolated.

Even if said regressions are happening because lazer behaves differently.  The mentioned issue has been active for _5_ years now.

This pr is a fix for a regression caused by my prior changes.
The "todo" isn't related to the issue I'm trying to resolve and is here because while this code works as expected right now, it won't be entirely correct when (or if) concurrent transforms handling will be adjusted to match stable.

But didn't the previous code already consider exactly the scenario @bdach is mentioning? It used `CommandsEndTime` which is `max(EndTime)`, and your optimised version changes that to the earliest time (or, now, the _last time provided_ in this PR)?

What I'm reading is a regression followed by a fix that regresses slightly less but is still a regression, is it not?
